profile.about: I am a software engineer with a degree in Game and around five years of professional Unity/C# game development experience, building gameplay, multiplayer, and reusable application systems. My recent work has expanded my production software engineering capabilities through enterprise architecture, API and data integration, and applied AI workflows using OCR, LLMs, structured output, validation, and normalization. My long-term direction is Game AI research, particularly adaptive companion agents, experience-driven character evolution, dynamic character progression, and AI systems that can adapt while remaining understandable and controllable by game designers.

research.statement: My primary interest is experience-driven character evolution: using structured gameplay history to influence both how a character behaves and how its abilities develop, while keeping the resulting system understandable, balanced, and designer-controllable.

direction.title: Experience-Driven Character Evolution
direction.workingTitle: A Shared Experience Model for Adaptive Behaviour and Skill Progression in RPG Companion Agents
direction.question: Can a shared representation of accumulated gameplay experience guide both companion behaviour adaptation and skill progression so that characters evolve in ways that reflect their actual gameplay histories?
direction.supportingStatement: The proposed RPG prototype records gameplay events and combat metrics and transforms them into a Character Experience Profile. The same representation is then used by both the behaviour system and the skill-progression system. Characters that begin from the same initial state but experience different gameplay conditions should gradually diverge in behaviour and abilities in ways that remain related to their histories rather than random variation.
